prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules bring a ubiquitin ligase and a chosen protein together to destroy it, through the PROTAC concept and the identification of cereblon as the target of molecular glue degraders

statement.case_for: After reading the full first-round exchange I have moved my preferred configuration from halide perovskites (B007) to targeted protein degradation (B020) with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The decisive point is that the scientific core is shared across independent readings: a small molecule induces a ligase-target ternary complex and event-driven, catalytic removal replaces occupancy-based inhibition. This is supported by ternary-complex structures, cooperativity and kinetics, and by reproduction in many groups, which is the evidence standard I applied to perovskites. As a structural chemist I find the ternary-complex structural work the most persuasive part, because it makes the principle a design discipline and not a list of compounds. The Crews-Deshaies concept and Handa's identification of cereblon explain two complementary halves of one mechanism, so one citation names a principle. Seven of eight opening ballots placed it in the top three, but that count is not my reason; my reason is that its attribution is far more defensible than any three-person split of the six perovskite names, which I could not resolve in round 1 and still cannot.
statement.case_against: No degrader is approved, so recognition rests on concept, mechanism and clinical pipeline rather than a delivered medicine, and the citation could be read as a compromise between two lineages with different inventors. The three-person limit excludes Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito, each with a credible claim; Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands in particular are close to what I find most convincing. There is also Brzezinski's point that this may read as medicinal chemistry or pharmacology that Medicine could claim. By contrast, perovskites remain an important materials-chemistry advance with unresolved stability and lead toxicity, and a materials prize deserves consideration if B020 attribution cannot be settled.

responses.point: Linke argues that PROTACs and cereblon glues converge on one ternary-complex principle, so a single citation with Crews, Deshaies and Handa honours both without stretching into two prizes.
responses.response: In round 1 I said your trio left out Ciulli and the glue chemistry. Your framing answers the second part, because the citation names the shared mechanism and not a compound list. I still regard the omission of Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito as a real cost, but your argument that the principle can be credited without declaring them non-contributors is acceptable to me, and I now support your configuration.

responses.point: Aqvist proposes Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli with a citation limited to bifunctional degraders, and holds that a glue-inclusive citation would blur the chemistry.
responses.response: I take the structural argument for Ciulli seriously, since ternary-complex design is what I find most convincing. But a citation limited to bifunctionals leaves the cereblon mechanism, the clearest molecular explanation in the field, uncredited. Handa also has a clean priority event, the 2010 identification of cereblon, whereas Ciulli's contribution is a design refinement of a concept already in place. I would rather put Ciulli among the first names omitted than split the committee over the third seat, though I would not block your version if it gained more votes.

responses.point: Chabes pairs base editing (Liu) with Crews and Deshaies, arguing the two parts honour distinct advances in how chemistry acts on biological macromolecules.
responses.response: In round 1 I said I would not argue against a single-person Liu prize, and I still think Liu's attribution is clean. But your two-part design also drops the cereblon strand, which is the pillar of the glue mechanism, and the 2020 CRISPR proximity and the Kondo-Nishida claim remain open. I prefer a single, well-defined B020 prize to a combination whose second part has these open questions, and I keep B047 as an alternative.

responses.point: Aili moved from Ciulli to Handa, arguing that a prize covering both heterobifunctional degraders and the glue mechanism is more coherent.
responses.response: You answered my round-1 worry. I said the PROTAC versus glue split resembled my own attribution problem with perovskites and would favour B020 only with a Crews-Deshaies-Handa or two-name configuration. Your reasoning that cereblon turns thalidomide-type drugs from a clinical accident into an understood mechanism gives that configuration its rationale, so I am joining it.

responses.point: Brzezinski concedes that the B020 attribution is easier than his own first choice, nitrogenase, and flags that B020 could equally be claimed by Medicine.
responses.response: I accept the Medicine overlap and think the citation should emphasise the chemical principle, induced proximity through a designed ternary complex and the molecular basis of cereblon recognition, which is where chemical and structural work is decisive. I note I am a Stockholm colleague of yours and I did not rely on that in moving; my change is based on the attribution reasoning above.

responses.point: Somfai prefers Buchwald and Hartwig for C-N coupling as the cleanest two-name attribution, while naming B020 and B047 as alternatives.
responses.response: I accept that attribution for B044 is cleaner, but the overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize and Kosugi's earlier work are objections you raise yourself. Since you name B020 as your first alternative, I think the committee can reach a configuration you could accept.

uncertainties: Whether Handa, Ciulli or no third name is the best seat; I cannot resolve the priority details beyond my memory.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader should delay the prize by a year.
Whether the Chemistry committee can defend B020 against a Medicine claim by emphasising the chemical principle.
I have not independently verified the 2001 PROTAC and 2010 cereblon priority dates, nor the perovskite sequence.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to any proposed laureate on B020 or the alternatives B007 and B047. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski and would not vote on that basis. My field, electron crystallography of porous materials, touches no shortlisted topic.
